english_verification.review_scope: Checked current English Mod country localisation, idea definitions, and representative mission passages; read the two fixed offline Wiki chunks listed above. No exhaustive mission audit was performed.

Formation reachability and all mission effects were not exhaustively audited.

rationale.colonization: Mountain expansion requires managing subterranean routes and open space.
rationale.complexity: The formation entrance, religious centre, hold levels, and spell flags are tightly coupled.
rationale.dark_story: Goblin purges and extreme exclusion are explicit in the text and script.
rationale.difficulty: Formation and late engineering require many prerequisites; no gameplay test was performed.
rationale.diplomacy: Isolationist diplomacy is written into the mission gates.
rationale.early_pressure: First retake the occupied hold from goblins while facing a major power to the east.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Runes, relics, and magical sanctuaries are the late-game core.
rationale.narrative_density: Ancient isolation, the 1439 fall, restoration, and renewed isolation form a complete main line.
rationale.tall_play: Holds, temples, fortifications, and relic engineering dominate the long campaign.
rationale.trade_economy: Resource supply supports engineering; this is not primarily a trade empire.
rationale.warfare: Retaking the hold and controlling the Tree of Stone create clear warfare stages.

identity.appearance: In 1444 the hold is held by the Chaingrasper Clan H74; a Dwarven adventurer can retake and restore I19.
identity.formation_scope: Take hold 4284 and meet the Dwarven adventurer restoration requirements, then change to I19 and receive its exclusive mission tree.
predecessors: A Dwarven adventurer able to retake the hold (no single predecessor Tag is required).

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas, and the ambition; excludes optional idea groups and racial or government bonuses. Candidate sets and conditions are listed separately and are not treated as simultaneous stacks; accepting a formation set depends on the actual event, decision, and player choice.

description.text: Ovdal-az-Ân was known in ancient Aul-Dwarov as the hold where faith and piety were cultivated, where every year thousands were educated in the ways of Gods. The most famed of these halls of education was the Hul-az-Dagrin, the Hall of Dagrin. Here the greatest minds were sent to learn theology, writing, and the best ways to exalt their gods of choice. Standards were strict, each body, mind, and soul carefully and exactingly measured. Flaws would not be tolerated and if they could not be hammered out upon the anvil of penance, those who bore them would be cast aside.

description.text: Vûrodrmonir is an ancient artefact, said to be a fragment of Joztralanna herself, the Goddess of the Moon and origin of magic, leftover from the creation of Dwarvenkind. Crafted by Urisazirn in an age long before Aul-Dwarov, Vûrodrmonir allows the wielder to cast powerful magics far beyond the ability of normal mages, so long as they are capable of magic themselves. Itself a sceptre, roughly three feet long, composed of an unknown metallic material that baffled any and all metallurgists who studied it, Vûrodrmonir was the possession of the High Priest of Halanna, their symbol of power, office, and reverence.

description.text: Where others faltered in their reverence of the Old Ways, the Granite Dwarves did not. When Ovdal Kanzad cast out the faithful, Ovdal-az-Ân welcomed them with open arms. As others began to wane in their devotion and faith, they did not abandon the Gods who had seen them through trial after trial, especially Halanna, mother of all dwarves. In so doing, they were rewarded with life, even as the impious around them burned. They hid the entry to their hold when the Tree of Stone was cast down for its heresy and so remained safe for millennia more. In the granite halls of Ovdal-az-Ân they dwelled, unmoving and eternal.

description.text: In 2203 BA, the legendary Odna II, both Queen of Ovdal-az-Ân and High Priestess of Halanna, ordered the sealing of Ovdal-az-Ân. This measure was not made lightly, but the heresy and dangers within the Tree of Stone were deemed extreme enough, to require such a drastic measure. A month-long period of solemn reflection was taken, during which time the hold's Runeworkers sealed the gate with specially runecarved granite blocks and Queen Odna used Vûrodrmonir to weave a complex spell over the gates. It was decreed, that the gates would only open again after 5,000 years had passed and the heretical world was once again safe for true believers. Thus did the Granite dwarves seal themselves off from the world, becoming as much a part of mother Halanna as the mountains themselves.

description.text: Hold Hogs are a type of Serpentspine creature, a distinctive breed of swine that was a staple meat of ancient Aul-Dwarov, and something Ovdal-az-Ân was famed for before the Fall. After their declaration of independence from the Jade Empire, many farmers in the hold sought to alleviate manpower and supply shortages by breeding larger and stockier hogs, more fit for hauling and pulling wagons. When an outbreak of Rotheflu decimated the hold's population of Rothe, it only further cemented Ovdal-az-Ân's reputation as a hold of swine with the rest of the Tree of Stone.

description.text: In the heart of Ovdal-az-Ân n sits a cavern of immense size, and at its heart an elegantly sculpted dagger of stone hangs from the ceiling. This is Argrâstun Cathedral, the centre of the cult of Halanna during the height of Aul-Dwarov. The stalactite, which Argrâstun Cathedral is made from, has been hollowed out into a massive temple complex dedicated to Halanna and is the seat of power from which the monarch ruled. Surrounded by dozens of other hanging temples to other gods, built from lesser stalagmites or stalactites that radiate out from it, the great cavern of Ovdal-az-Ân was a breathtaking site, with no part as wonderous or well adorned as Argrâstun.

description.text: In 1435 AA, the unthinkable occurred. The isolation that Ovdal-az-Ân had so long enjoyed was broken, as a horde of goblins broke through the long-unmanned gate, the illusion of Odna pierced by mere chance. Within hours, entire sections of the upper level were swarmed by goblins, who seemed more interested in taking dwarves as slaves than plundering. Thousands were captured before a proper defence could be mounted and even then, the mobilisation was slow. As the siege continued, more goblins were drawn to the hold and within a few short years, the hold of Ovdal-az-Ân had fallen. Only in the shadows did a few hardy souls remain, fighting an ever more desperate war for their survival.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you want to select a finished country directly in 1444 or do not want an isolationist purge theme.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Retake the hold and form I19, restore the hold and religious centre, then rule the mountains through runic fortresses and relic magic.
player_overview.overview: Ovdal-az-Ân is not an existing Dwarven country in 1444: the hold is in goblin hands, so a Dwarven adventurer must retake and rebuild it. The campaign then grows from ruined archives and Pantheon faith into hold construction, pilgrimage, and runic engineering, ultimately creating a powerful religious-magical state in the Tree of Stone. The price is a long formation and construction process, plus explicit goblin purges and extreme isolation.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy Dwarven holds, religious magic, and defensive construction campaigns.
signature_features: Retake the hold from the goblins and rebuild the country as an adventurer.
The Pantheon, runic fortifications, and sacred relics drive a magical engineering campaign.
The missions require isolationist diplomacy and turn the Tree of Stone into a defensive sanctuary.
player_overview.tagline: Retake the fallen Hold of One and forge religious heritage, runic magic, and mountain defences into a sealed sanctuary.

reasons: The lost hold and Pantheon revival create a clear historical arc
Relic magic and runic fortifications are highly distinctive
Defensive construction and religious expansion reinforce each other
warnings: I19 cannot be selected directly in 1444
Retaking the hold and later developing multiple holds takes time
Goblin purges and explicit isolationism are central themes

positive_indicators: Freeing Dwarves enslaved by the Command
Restoring education, pilgrimage, and hold infrastructure
values.rationale: The first mission directly enables a goblin purge, and the late narrative explicitly excludes non-kin. Education, freeing enslaved Dwarves, and hold construction provide limited positive evidence. The penalty concerns concrete purges and denial of personhood, not religion, isolation, or ordinary war.
red_flags: The missions enable a purge directed at goblins
The late state claims the mountains for its own-faith population only
